allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Let f_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum for integer k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n and reals t, if n > 1 and 0 ≤ t < 1, then 0 ≤ n*t and n*t < n.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n with n > 1 and every real number t with 0 ≤ t < 1, one has 0 ≤ n*t < n.

relied_only_on: order preservation under multiplication by a positive real number

result_payload.proof_nl: Let n be an integer with n > 1, and let t be a real number with 0 <= t < 1. Since n > 1, in particular n > 0. Multiplying the inequalities 0 <= t < 1 by the positive number n preserves their directions, giving 0 <= nt < n. This is exactly the desired conclusion.
result_payload.proof_summary: Because n is positive, multiplying 0 <= t < 1 by n yields 0 <= nt < n.
